To summarize, the key findings of our research, stated in one sentence that includes all relevant information, are that
7,12-DMBA forms depurination addducts with DNA in mouse skin in vivo and that the 12- CH3 group of 7, 12-DMA is the site at which DNA adduct formation occurs.
the 12-methylation of DMBA is essential for the formation of depurination addducts, which are responsible for the initiation step of carcinogenesis.
the depurination products of DMBA, namely, 12-CH2-7-methylbenzo[a]anthracenyl-N7-guanine and -adenine, are the major adducts formed by cytochromes P450 and peroxidases in mouse skin and in rat liver.
In summary, our research is concerned with
the identification and quantification of the depurinating and stable DNA adduction products of DMBA formed by the one-electron oxidation of DMBA by P450.
the identification and characterization of DNA adducts formed during the metabolism of polycyclic aromatic hydrocarbons (PAH).
the chemical carcinogens and the mechanism of carcinogenesis.
In summary, a comprehensive and detailed conclusive statement would be that
the depurination DNA lesions are not the result of a chemical reaction between DNA and DMBA, but the result of a one electron transfer from DNA to the DMBA molecule.

the 7,12-Dimethylbenzanthracene (7,12-DMBA), a carcinogen, is a substrate for the P450 system.
